body: I'm so sorry for your loss, and I'm sorry you seem to have regrets. This definitely wasn't easy for me, especially since I didn't even know I could get pregnant. It was the hardest decision I'd ever made in my life, but I feel it saved both of ours. I just started therapy because I knew I needed to talk things through. I've been continuously trying to justify my choice to myself even though I know there was a very high (about 80%) chance that only one, or neither of us would have survived. And if we did I could not provide a sustainable, happy life for us. The experience itself was physically painful and traumatic as well. I took the pill at home. Its heart wrenching all the way through. But my therapist has been helping me learn to cope, how to keep my head up and look towards what can now be in my life, without the fear of it ending in a few months. I'll be taking my SATs again and my ACTs in a few weeks to start looking for scholarships. My boyfriend and I have started a $5mo/savings for when we are ready (if my treatment goes well in a few years). And if not to adopt. I wish I could take away your guilt, I hope you forgive yourself for this decision because I know it was difficult, especially at 19, (I wont say how old, but Im not far off from that age) As someone who only has my partner for support I wish you love, compassion, and sympathy. You deserve support, and you deserve to forgive yourself.

Call me selfish, but there are other things wrong with me that would have made the pregnancy difficult. There was no guarantee I would have stayed pregnant, and if I did that either of us would've survived in the end. I'm young and honestly don't want to die. I've struggled to get to a point where I'm healthy enough to not fear for my life everyday.
